summary: Summit lookout on Big Huckleberry Mountain: a 1920s cab, a 1931 L-4 cab, then gone. Only anchors, glass and cable were reported later.

facts.design: Cab from the 1920s, replaced in 1931 by an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: The L-4 cab is gone. Willhite found guy-line anchors, glass and cable on the summit; he could not date its destruction.

access.note: Reached on foot by trail. WTA mentions a rough road approach, provided you are OK with it. Gate or closure status not stated.

visit.trail_note: Short spur trail to the summit, branching off the Pacific Crest Trail (Willhite; WTA describes a steep, undulating trail).

events.note: Weebly index says the site was developed as a lookout point; FFLOS dates the first cab to the 1920s
L-4 cab placed on the summit, replacing the 1920s cab
A Geodetic Survey team mentioned the lookout
Registered as US 1307, WA 207 on June 23, 2012

evidence.supports: Cab built in the 1920s replaced by an L-4 cab in 1931; L-4 now gone
evidence.quote: A cab built in the 1920s was replaced in 1931 with an L-4 cab, which is now gone.

evidence.supports: Cab in the 1920s, L-4 in 1931, now gone
Site developed as a lookout point in 1920
evidence.quote: 1920: This site was developed as a lookout point.
July 9, 1941: Panorama photos taken by Reinhardt.

evidence.supports: L-4 placed on top in 1931; little remains
evidence.quote: in 1931 a L-4 cab was placed on top, not much remains but some guy line anchors, glass and cable

evidence.supports: Little is known about the lookout
evidence.quote: Not much is known about the old fire lookout that was on the summit.

evidence.supports: Geodetic Survey mention in 1946; date of destruction unclear
evidence.quote: A Geodetic Survey team mentioned the lookout in 1946, but its unclear when it was destroyed.

evidence.supports: Summit on the divide between Panther Creek and the Little White Salmon River
evidence.quote: Big Huckleberry Mountain is on the divide between Panther Creek and the Little White Salmon River

evidence.supports: Location just north of the Columbia Gorge Scenic Area
evidence.quote: just north of the Columbia Gorge Scenic Area

evidence.supports: Short spur trail branches off the Pacific Crest Trail to the summit
evidence.quote: the side trail that branches off 1/4 mile to the summit

evidence.supports: WTA calls the summit another former fire lookout site
evidence.quote: another site of a former fire lookout

evidence.supports: Short spur trail to the summit
evidence.quote: onto a short spur trail to the summit

evidence.supports: Views still quite good but less wide than at Grassy Knoll
evidence.quote: the views from here aren't quite as all-encompassing as down at Grassy Knoll, but they're still quite good.

evidence.supports: Trail is a steep, undulating path
evidence.quote: the trail to Big Huckleberry Mountain is a steep, undulating path

evidence.supports: WTA mentions a rough road approach, provided you are OK with it
evidence.quote: provided you're OK with a rough road approach

evidence.supports: L-4 is a 14 by 14 foot frame cab that could be placed atop tall firetowers
evidence.quote: 14'x14' frame cabs were made to live in and could be placed atop tall firetowers.

sources.title: Big Huckleberry Mountain - Gifford Pinchot National Forest

notes_for_editor: Thin record: no staffing, fire or demolition date found, and Willhite's page gives no date for his visit. The brief's status 'gone' and county Skamania hold up. Access is inferred from WTA's trail description; gate status is not checked. Do not confuse with the separate Little Huckleberry Mountain lookout site.
